3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: My motorcade traveled for over an hour before the Archsanctuary of Plavo appeared on the horizon. Its golden dome radiated under the sunrise.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: It was a view I’d seen countless times, but it never failed to inspire awe.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: It was a view that inspired awe in many a Rizian, especially the most devout followers of St. Wruhec.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: Titus, who was sitting next to the driver, turned back to me.

7.speaker: Titus Gordion
7.text: "We shall be arriving shortly, Your Majesty."

8.speaker: Player_Romus
8.text: "Good. I’ve been looking forward to this for quite some time."

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: I was here for the Consecration of the King, the centuries-old ecclesiastical ceremony symbolizing a monarch's appointment as God’s highest representative on earth.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: Better known as the “divine right of kings.”

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: Unlike my coronation, this was a private event shrouded in secrecy.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: Not even my father, despite my asking, would disclose what occurred. He'd simply say, “What took place was between me and God.”

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: But aside from the pomp and circumstance of the Consecration of the King, this meeting was my chance to catch up on Rizia's current state of religious affairs.

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: Before long, my car pulled up in front of the towering colonnades situated on either side of the entrance.

17.speaker: Player_Romus
17.text: "Grand Wiseman Ignacius... looking as stoic as ever."

18.speaker: Player_Romus
18.text: "Look at the old geezer. Hard to believe he's still breathing."

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: While most shouted my praises, there was a small group of demonstrators protesting against the ceremony.

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: A welcoming smile spread across the Grand Wiseman's face as he came down the stairs.

22.speaker: Sal Ignacius
22.text: "Welcome, Your Majesty. We are greatly honored to have you here for this momentous occasion."

23.speaker: Sal Ignacius
23.text: "I look forward to serving you just as I served your father.”

24.speaker: Player_Romus
24.text: "It is I who is honored to be here."

25.speaker: Player_Romus
25.text: "I shall honor this day with the dignity and respect this sacred tradition deserves."

26.speaker: Player_Romus
26.text: "I could think of better ways to spend my day. But when duty calls, one must oblige."

27.speaker: Sal Ignacius
27.text: “It fills my heart with joy to hear it.”

28.speaker: Sal Ignacius
28.text: "I shall do my best to provide you with both personal and state guidance on religion.”

29.speaker: Player_Romus
29.text: “Thank you, Grand Wiseman. I aspire to fulfill God's will here on earth, just as you have done."

30.speaker: Player_Romus
30.text: “Time is short, Grand Wiseman. Let us skip the pleasantries."

31.speaker: Player_Romus
31.text: "And I am privileged to receive your guidance.”

32.speaker: Player_Romus
32.text: "Your best? Only the weak whine about doing their best."

33.speaker: Sal Ignacius
33.text: "I'm merely a humble servant, Your Grace. I do as God commands."

34.speaker: Sal Ignacius
34.text: “The six stars of St. Wruhec still shine upon our nation."

35.speaker: Sal Ignacius
35.text: “Come, let us step inside. We have much to discuss.”

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: We began heading toward the entrance. However, I didn't get very far before my attention was drawn to a commotion from behind.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: As I turned to look, a throng of people surged against my security guards.

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: Titus, without missing a beat, caught the man by the arm and threw him to the ground. Other guards approached as Titus held him down.

42.speaker: Player_Romus
42.text: “And so you banned them. Rightly so, I might add."

43.speaker: Player_Romus
43.text: “Could we not have built Golcondist sanctuaries to pacify them?”

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: With a nod from Captain Gordion, two of his guardsmen lifted the man to his feet and escorted him away.

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: Sal and I continued towards the archsanctuary's entrance.

46.speaker: Sal Ignacius
46.text: "I humbly apologize for the interruption, Your Majesty."

49.speaker: Player_Romus
49.text: “Yes. The sooner we get this over with, the better.”

51.speaker: Player_Romus
51.text: "Just point me in the right direction."

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: I accompanied Sal into the archsanctuary. Titus and one of his men stood guard at the entrance.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: Our footsteps echoed throughout the massive empty chamber as we made our way down the main aisle that separated the hall in two.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: I was surrounded by ornate wall murals of religious scene depictions, leaving no surface bare. Nearby statues seemed to watch me as I passed.

55.speaker: Sal Ignacius
55.text: “It’s only fitting that such a monument be built atop the final resting place of Rizia's most revered disciple."

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: “I remember the archsanctuary being a lot bigger.”

58.speaker: Player_Romus
58.text: “One could get lost in a place like this.”

60.speaker: Sal Ignacius
60.text: "Some might say that spiritual sustenance comes from within."

61.speaker: Sal Ignacius
61.text: "Caelus the Devout. Singlehandedly credited for spreading the teachings of St. Wruhec throughout our part of the world."

62.speaker: Player_Romus
62.text: “I’m not here for a history lesson. Let’s get down to business.”

63.speaker: Player_Romus
63.text: "As a great admirer of his, I've always aspired to lead a life of devotion and virtue, much like his own."

65.speaker: Player_Romus
65.text: “Yes, yes. I know all about him. But he’s not the reason why I’m here.”

66.speaker: Sal Ignacius
66.text: "It warms my heart to hear it."

67.speaker: Sal Ignacius
67.text: "Without him, we Rizians would be no more enlightened than Dastnurists."

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: We stopped when we'd reached the chancel where the altar stood.

69.speaker: Player_Romus
69.text: "As long as you are Grand Wiseman, I'm sure those values will persevere."

70.speaker: Player_Romus
70.text: "The Dastnurists are particularly concerning. Their religion disregards the centuries of progress since Descension Day."

71.speaker: Player_Romus
71.text: "The Golcondists pose a particularly large threat, using Wruhecism as a cover for blasphemy."

72.speaker: Player_Romus
72.text: "I wouldn't call it 'diluted.' Supporting a plurality of religions will only enrich Rizian culture."

73.speaker: Sal Ignacius
73.text: "But we must not lose sight of our one true faith."

74.speaker: Sal Ignacius
74.text: "However, he was also deluged with requests from the Dastnurist community. In particular, the Grandsanctuary of Sallabes has long been too small to serve worshippers' needs and is urgently in need of expansion."

75.speaker: Player_Romus
75.text: “Why is it the government's responsibility to fund sanctuaries? Couldn't Rizia's religious congregations pay for their own repairs and expansions?"

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "Why didn't he just fund both projects?"

77.speaker: Player_Romus
77.text: "We will begin the restoration of Plavo at once." [-2 Budget]

78.speaker: Player_Romus
78.text: "Both projects are equally important in my eyes. I will speak to Elena about funding both the Plavo restoration and the Sallabes Grandsanctuary expansion.” [-4 Budget]

79.speaker: Player_Romus
79.text: "Serving the Dastnurist community should take priority at this time. I will grant the Archpriest of Sallabes' request." [-2 Budget]

80.speaker: Sal Ignacius
80.text: “I see the wisdom in your decision. May God’s shining light forever guide you even through the darkest times.”

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: The holy man let out a small gasp.

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: Sal spread his arms wide open.

85.speaker: Sal Ignacius
85.text: “With great honor, I shall lead you as you step across the threshold and unite with the divine."

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: He motioned toward a stone archway leading out of the chamber.

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: I followed the Grand Wiseman down a long corridor.

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: I continued after him as we went down the stairs, which seemed to go on forever.

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: Before long, we'd reached the bottom, where I was greeted by a wall of human bones that were carefully stacked from top to bottom.

91.speaker: Player_Romus
91.text: “I had no idea this was down here.”

93.speaker: Sal Ignacius
93.text: "As for the tomb's tenants, they're mostly wealthy noblemen and their families alongside other well-to-do individuals throughout the centuries."

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: As we made our way down the tunnel, the ceiling began to close in around us, and feelings of claustrophobia began to sink in.

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: Just when it seemed like the tunnel would never end, we emerged into a vast cavern, also illuminated by torchlight. Several wiscerers, lesser in rank than Sal, were waiting for us.

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: They were arranged around a marble sarcophagus.

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: “Is that who I think it is?"

99.speaker: Sal Ignacius
99.text: "Rare are those who have set foot here. Count yourself among the blessed few."

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: Caelus the Devout's effigy became more apparent as I approached.

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: Sal placed his torch into a nearby sconce as one of the other wisemen, carrying a silver tray, approached us.

102.speaker: Narrator
102.text: On it was a golden chalice, a clay jug filled with oil, a sponge, and what appeared to be a bottle of wine.

103.speaker: Sal Ignacius
103.text: “Let us begin. Please remove your clothes and stand on the royal seal.”

106.speaker: Player_Romus
106.text: “Actually... I'm beginning to have second thoughts."

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: Following the Grand Wiseman's instructions, I joined him in reciting verses from the sacred scripture.

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: When my garments were completely removed, Sal proceeded to anoint me, dipping a sponge into the fragrant oil and gently applying it all over my body.

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: He then poured the wine into the chalice until it reached the brim.

110.speaker: Sal Ignacius
110.text: “It is well known that this is the final resting place of Caelus the Devout."

111.speaker: Sal Ignacius
111.text: "But what most don’t know is that this is where he performed his first miracle.”

113.speaker: Player_Romus
113.text: “I’ve never heard of disciples performing miracles before.”

114.speaker: Player_Romus
114.text: “I have gone along with you thus far. But are you really saying something supernatural happened here?"

115.speaker: Player_Romus
115.text: “Even as a religious man, I have trouble believing in miracles."

117.speaker: Sal Ignacius
117.text: "For upon filling his stomach with the sacred wine -- the very wine before you now -- he was given the ability to prophesy the future."

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: He poured the wine into the chalice and held it high.

120.speaker: Sal Ignacius
120.text: "You will see nothing. Only the most pious and reverent men may drink from the sacred chalice."

121.speaker: Sal Ignacius
121.text: "You see, once this wine is consumed, Caelus the Devout's gift of foresight shall, for a time, be bestowed upon the person who ingests it."

122.speaker: Narrator
122.text: He held up the chalice, once more, and drank until the wine was gone.

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: Setting it back down on the tray, he then stepped toward me and held out his hands.

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: We stood there in silence for what felt like an eternity. I wasn't sure what to expect.

125.speaker: Narrator
125.text: But then suddenly, his body began to tremble and his hands took a firm grip in mine.

126.speaker: Sal Ignacius
126.text: "Listen closely to my words. For the gift of sight comes in flashes."

133.speaker: Sal Ignacius
133.text: "To consummate the Consecration of the King I must insist that you take my hands."

135.speaker: Player_Romus
135.text: "Nobody told me there would be prophecies. I cannot govern with the burden of future events looming over me."

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "And *I* must insist you remember who you're speaking to!"

137.speaker: Sal Ignacius
137.text: "I must insist that you take my hand, or else I cannot bestow my consent on the ceremony's completion."

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: I quickly put on my clothes and made my way back through the catacombs until I'd reached the surface.

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: Titus and another guardsman were at my side the moment they saw me re-emerge.

141.speaker: Player_Romus
141.text: "That's none of your concern. We're leaving."

144.speaker: Player_Romus
144.text: "Get out of my way, Captain. Do you want to be demoted to private?"

145.speaker: Narrator
145.text: I thought about the Grand Wiseman's last words to me as the Archsanctuary of Plavo faded from view.

146.speaker: Narrator
146.text: Before long, my motorcade was back on the road.

147.speaker: Narrator
147.text: By the time I'd made it back to the car, the captain was so far behind, I ended up opening the door myself.

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: I barely noticed when the motorcade pulled out of the city and back onto the highway.

149.speaker: Narrator
149.text: I couldn't let go even if I wanted.

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: My outburst left the wiseman speechless. Seemingly shocked, he bowed his head and backed away.

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: At his advanced age, he wasn't exactly spry.

153.speaker: Player_Romus
153.text: "I should be the one asking you."

155.speaker: Player_Romus
155.text: "As best as one can be, given the situation."

158.speaker: Sal Ignacius
158.text: "I hope I'm not overstepping my bounds. But it was a situation that, unfortunately, should never have happened in the first place--"

159.speaker: Sal Ignacius
159.text: "Can't say the same for myself. These old bones don't move as quickly as they used to."

160.speaker: Sal Ignacius
160.text: "Oh, I may have some years on me, but I'm not dead yet."

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: He closed his eyes and began taking in long deep breaths.

163.speaker: Sal Ignacius
163.text: "I see a crown. It's ascending into the sky... rising high above the surrounding countryside--"

164.speaker: Player_Romus
164.text: "I know this may seem highly unorthodox, but this whole secret ceremony just doesn't sit well with me."

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "I must break with the archaic customs of my predecessors if I am to be the ruler Rizia needs right now."

166.speaker: Sal Ignacius
166.text: "A sovereign leader of this great nation you’re duty-bound to uphold this sacred tradition, just as all the monarchs who came before you."

167.speaker: Sal Ignacius
167.text: "The crown you wear isn't just a decorative headdress, but a symbol of national identity -- of unity and pride."

168.speaker: Sal Ignacius
168.text: "It represents stability and steadfast continuity even through the darkest of times."

169.speaker: Sal Ignacius
169.text: "My point is that you not only embody a kingdom on earth, but the kingdom above."

170.speaker: Player_Romus
170.text: "What does this diatribe have anything to do with my taking part in the ceremony?"

171.speaker: Player_Romus
171.text: "I'm well aware of what the crown represents. Please get to the point."

172.speaker: Player_Romus
172.text: "Yes, and I am grateful for the responsibility bestowed upon me."

175.speaker: Sal Ignacius
175.text: "You not only embody a kingdom on earth, but the kingdom above."

177.speaker: Sal Ignacius
177.text: "And I, for one, am grateful for having you as our king. As are the millions of subjects under your rule."

178.speaker: Sal Ignacius
178.text: "For to reject the sacrament is to reject God himself."

179.speaker: Player_Romus
179.text: "By that logic, a challenge to your King is a challenge to the Almighty."

180.speaker: Player_Romus
180.text: "You're right. Please forgive me. The crown's weight is heavy, and only with God's guidance can I fulfill my duties."

181.speaker: Player_Romus
181.text: "Religion's place in society is without question. But as for its role in government... I have reservations."

184.speaker: Narrator
184.text: The wiscerer went silent. Though he outwardly remained calm, the disdain in his eyes told a different story.

185.speaker: Player_Romus
185.text: "I'm glad you brought this to my attention, but I'd rather not make an immediate decision. I'll think it over once I'm back at the Palace."

186.speaker: Sal Ignacius
186.text: "With all due respect to the Golden Guard."

187.speaker: Sal Ignacius
187.text: "Wruhecism and the Rizian monarchy are one and the same. It has been that way since the beginning."

188.speaker: Sal Ignacius
188.text: "This kingdom has been blessed for a reason. Any change to the status quo will surely jeopardize our prosperity."

189.speaker: Player_Romus
189.text: "You make a valid point. I'm still not fully sold on religion's role in government, however, I know better than to upset that delicate balance."

190.speaker: Player_Romus
190.text: "Religion and state should be separate. End of story."

191.speaker: Player_Romus
191.text: "I believe my position on this issue is unlikely to change. But I see no obstacle to finding common ground if the opportunity arises."

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: Sal gasped in astonishment as I made an about-face and headed back towards the catacombs.

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: I could still smell the "holy oil" permeating off of me.

198.speaker: Sal Ignacius
198.text: "Does this mean you'll go through with the consecration?"

199.speaker: Player_Romus
199.text: "If that's what it takes to get your blessing, then yes."

200.speaker: Player_Romus
200.text: "No, but since I did agree to reallocate funds toward the Archsanctuary of Plavo as well as the Dastnurist Grand Sanctuary, perhaps we can overlook my abstention?"

201.speaker: Player_Romus
201.text: "No, but since I did agree to reallocate funds toward the Dastnurist Grand Sanctuary, perhaps we can overlook my abstention?"
201.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_PlavoSanctuaryRestoration_Project"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_SallabesSanctuaryExpansion_Project"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_SallabesSanctuaryExpansion_Project"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_PlavoSanctuaryRestoration_Project"] == true) == false)

202.speaker: Sal Ignacius
202.text: "The importance of the ceremony cannot be overstated."

209.speaker: Player_Romus
209.text: "No, but since I did agree to reallocate funds toward the Archsanctuary of Plavo, perhaps we can overlook my abstention?"
209.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_PlavoSanctuaryRestoration_Project"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_SallabesSanctuaryExpansion_Project"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_PlavoSanctuaryRestoration_Project"] == true)

214.speaker: Sal Ignacius
214.text: "As long as similar... *arrangements* can be made in the future."

215.speaker: Player_Romus
215.text: "No promises, but my door is always open to further discussions."

216.speaker: Player_Romus
216.text: "This was a one-time agreement. Be grateful you got any concessions at all."

217.speaker: Sal Ignacius
217.text: "Excellent. I look forward to a prosperous relationship in the future."

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: I wished Wiseman Ignacius goodbye and left the premises. Captain Gordion and his men followed behind.

219.speaker: Narrator
219.text: As my motorcade traveled down the highway, and the Archsacturary of Plavo faded from view, I reflected on all I had accomplished today.

220.speaker: Narrator
220.text: And hoped my future relationship with the wiscerer would remain amicable.

221.speaker: Sal Ignacius
221.text: "Very well then. I will, of course, remain hopeful that you'll have a change of heart."

222.speaker: Narrator
222.text: I bid Wiseman Ignacius farewell and departed the premises, with Captain Gordion and his men following closely behind.

223.speaker: Narrator
223.text: As my motorcade journeyed down the highway, the Archsacturary of Plavo slowly disappearing from sight, I reflected on all I had achieved today.

224.speaker: Narrator
224.text: The wiscerer knew his place now. I just hoped he wouldn't need friendly *reminders* in the future.

226.speaker: Sal Ignacius
226.text: "If I may give you a piece of advice..."

229.speaker: Player_Romus
229.text: "Fine. But hurry it up. I haven't got all day."

231.speaker: Sal Ignacius
231.text: "The throne you have inherited bestows great advantages, yet it also brings forth numerous adversities."

232.speaker: Sal Ignacius
232.text: "It would be a shame if any unnecessary strains or hostilities were added to your troubles."

234.speaker: Player_Romus
234.text: "And if I may give *you* a piece of advice... the door swings both ways."

235.speaker: Player_Romus
235.text: "You forget your place, Grand Wiseman. The onus lies not on the king to seek favor with others, but rather, it is others who should seek favor with the king."

236.speaker: Player_Romus
236.text: "Duly noted. I will take my leave. Good day."

237.speaker: Sal Ignacius
237.text: "Heavens no! I'm simply saying... tread carefully."

239.speaker: Sal Ignacius
239.text: "Well, in any case, I'm glad you're here."

240.speaker: Sal Ignacius
240.text: "Don't let my physical frailty fool you, Your Majesty. For the grace of God gives me unimaginable strength."

241.speaker: Player_Romus
241.text: "Good. That's what I like to hear."

249.speaker: Player_Romus
249.text: "I'm sorry, but I can't. This is too much."

250.speaker: Sal Ignacius
250.text: "And on the crown is a fracture on the golden band..."

255.speaker: Sal Ignacius
255.text: "The higher it journeys upward, the larger the crack gets."

256.speaker: Sal Ignacius
256.text: "Whether or not it can be mended is uncertain."

260.speaker: Sal Ignacius
260.text: "The visions are possible outcomes of what could come to pass. They aren't set in stone."

266.speaker: Sal Ignacius
266.text: "I now see soldiers... Many soldiers... War... And death. So much death."

271.speaker: Narrator
271.text: I continued to listen closely to his words.

272.speaker: Sal Ignacius
272.text: "I now see two individuals... They are embraced in each other's arms... Lovers."

273.speaker: Sal Ignacius
273.text: "Before me now is a heart... it's being stabbed by a sword."

276.speaker: Player_Romus
276.text: "This is starting to sound like utter nonsense."

277.speaker: Sal Ignacius
277.text: "Now, I behold an endless sea of people stretching as far as the eye can see... They are marching toward the royal palace... in joy or anger... I can not say for sure."

278.speaker: Sal Ignacius
278.text: "Above them are birds... tens of thousands of them so thick they blacken the sky... They are migrating from distant lands and making their nest in ours..."

279.speaker: Player_Romus
279.text: "It's obvious that the birds represent Wehzek Dastnurists coming to our lands."

280.speaker: Player_Romus
280.text: "The birds clearly represent Golcondists coming to our lands."

281.speaker: Player_Romus
281.text: "It sounds to me like they represent literal birds."

282.speaker: Sal Ignacius
282.text: "And on a nearby mountain overlooking the city sits a beast... a beast with three heads. Each head is fighting with the other..."

283.speaker: Sal Ignacius
283.text: "They must be brought under control, either through taming or severing one or more heads..."

285.speaker: Player_Romus
285.text: "Rizia's royal houses. Toras, Sazon and Azaro."

286.speaker: Player_Romus
286.text: "As it stands, Rizian lands are ruled under three different flags... Wehlen, The Grand Duchy of Pales, and our own... That could be the meaning..."

287.speaker: Player_Romus
287.text: "Alright. I've heard enough of this bullshit. Let me go."

288.speaker: Narrator
288.text: I felt Sal loosen his hold of me, letting go.

292.speaker: Narrator
292.text: I opened my eyes and looked at him curiously until he finally spoke.

293.speaker: Narrator
293.text: I looked at him curiously until he finally spoke.

294.speaker: Sal Ignacius
294.text: "The visions have stopped. Thus, concluding the ceremony."

296.speaker: Player_Romus
296.text: "Wait... I have so many questions I want to ask."

298.speaker: Narrator
298.text: A part of me questioned whether or not what I'd experienced was real.

299.speaker: Sal Ignacius
299.text: "I don't have the answer you're looking for. It's now up to you to decipher their meaning."

300.speaker: Sal Ignacius
300.text: "Good. For it's now up to you to decipher their meaning."

301.speaker: Sal Ignacius
301.text: "Give it time. Their meaning will come to you soon enough. It's up to you to decipher them."

303.speaker: Sal Ignacius
303.text: "It's not uncommon to have feelings of doubt. It's now up to you to decipher the meaning of said visions."

304.speaker: Narrator
304.text: After a long moment, during which he seemed to still be recovering, he spoke again.

305.speaker: Narrator
305.text: Before long, I was back on the road again -- back to reality.

306.speaker: Narrator
306.text: As the Archsanctuary of Plavo faded from view, and my mind began to settle, I thought more about the visions, and what they meant.

308.speaker: Narrator
308.text: At the heart of the room stood a circle of six columns, each bearing a single star delicately carved upon them.

309.speaker: Narrator
309.text: And if they were real, what my next steps should be.

310.speaker: Narrator
310.text: Security guards held back a crowd of onlookers gathered along either side of the stairway leading up to the archsanctuary, where the Grand Wiseman stood.

316.speaker: Narrator
316.text: "Divus zaitu" was Wruhecist for "May God be with you."

319.speaker: Titus Gordion
319.text: "Of course. My most sincere apologies, Your Majesty."

325.speaker: Player_Romus
325.text: "Personal commentary isn't a part of your job description."

326.speaker: Titus Gordion
326.text: "You're right. I was out of line. My apologies."

327.speaker: Player_Romus
327.text: "I'm pleased to know that our opinions align."

328.speaker: Player_Romus
328.text: "I couldn't agree more. As long as his loyalty remains steadfast."

330.speaker: Player_Romus
330.text: "Excuse my bluntness. I apologize if I offended you."

336.speaker: Sal Ignacius
336.text: "After today, it shall be you who speaks for the Divine."

337.speaker: Sal Ignacius
337.text: "As the Lord's representative on earth, I expect nothing less."

340.speaker: Sal Ignacius
340.text: "That's because you used to be a lot smaller. Memories of you first learning to walk are as vivid in my mind as if they were yesterday."

341.speaker: Sal Ignacius
341.text: "Indeed it does. I've been here more times than I can remember and still get choked up sometimes."

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: I suddenly recalled how overjoyed I was to see Vina take her first steps.

345.speaker: Sal Ignacius
345.text: "However, there are those who need a little spectacle to ignite that internal spark. This magnificent sanctuary serves that purpose."

346.speaker: Sal Ignacius
346.text: "That is of course worrying, Your Majesty."

348.speaker: Sal Ignacius
348.text: "I agree, Your Majesty, but King Valero was hesitant to let go of such a large sum at once."

349.speaker: Sal Ignacius
349.text: "So you'll go through with the ceremony?"

353.speaker: Sal Ignacius
353.text: "'Second thoughts?' But you have to go through with it!"

355.speaker: Player_Romus
355.text: "It is the holiest of honors to be allowed here."

356.speaker: Sal Ignacius
356.text: “Why, Caelus the Devout, of course. The reason for this Archsanctuary's very existence."

357.speaker: Sal Ignacius
357.text: "Indeed, Your Majesty. This is the tomb of Caelus the Devout."

358.speaker: Sal Ignacius
358.text: "A most vicious foe. More than that, I cannot say."

359.speaker: Sal Ignacius
359.text: "One of the armies, yes. Their uniforms carry the royal seal."

363.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll

(Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Rel_Who_Is_The_Victor"] == true  or

376.speaker: Sal Ignacius
376.text: "One of them is of your blood."

381.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
381.conditionsRaw:
(Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Religion_LoversGoOn"] == true  or

396.speaker: Sal Ignacius
396.text: "It's a forbidden love or one of disapproval."

399.speaker: Sal Ignacius
399.text: "They are surrounded by people both for and against their union."

402.speaker: Sal Ignacius
402.text: "I can assure you, Your Grace, my visions are anything *but* nonsense."

403.speaker: Sal Ignacius
403.text: "If true, it could mean dark clouds on the horizon are fast approaching."

406.speaker: Sal Ignacius
406.text: "Please do, Your Majesty. The spiritual health of our kingdom is at stake."

411.speaker: Narrator
411.text: The Grand Wiseman clapped his hands together.

412.speaker: Sal Ignacius
412.text: "Excellent, Your Majesty! I look forward to seeing these pews lined with worshippers once more!"

413.speaker: Titus Gordion
413.text: "We'll take it from here, Your Majesty."

415.speaker: Player_Romus
415.text: "It seems I misjudged you after all, Captain Gordion. You have my thanks."

416.speaker: Player_Romus
416.text: "Oh, now you'll 'take it from here?' He should have never broken through your men in the first place."

417.speaker: Titus Gordion
417.text: "Please accept my apology. It won't happen again."

418.speaker: Narrator
418.text: The surprise visitor was shouting something, but I couldn't understand what he was saying.

419.speaker: Player_Romus
419.text: "What? Did you expect me to handle it myself?"

420.speaker: Titus Gordion
420.text: "No. Of course not. I'll have this taken care of right away."

421.speaker: Titus Gordion
421.text: "It is my honor. My men will deal with this rogue accordingly."

422.speaker: Player_Romus
422.text: "Was that man who I think he was?"

423.speaker: Player_Romus
423.text: "Can't say I cared for that little stunt, but I do wonder what the man wanted."

424.speaker: Player_Romus
424.text: "I'll see to it that the protester is locked away for quite some time."

425.speaker: Player_Romus
425.text: "Quite the daredevil, that man. I'm inclined to know his motivation."

426.speaker: Sal Ignacius
426.text: "I believe he was a Derdian Golcondist. He was wearing their traditional garb."

427.speaker: Sal Ignacius
427.text: "Judging by his wardrobe, he appeared to be a Derdian Golcondist."

428.speaker: Sal Ignacius
428.text: "He was a Derdian Golcondist. I'd say his motivation was clear."

429.speaker: Sal Ignacius
429.text: "Plavo is one of the holiest places in all of Wruhecism. A belief that the Golcondists *claim* to hold."

430.speaker: Sal Ignacius
430.text: "There was a time when Golcondists prayed here in such small numbers that their presence was tolerated."

431.speaker: Narrator
431.text: We continued towards the archsanctuary's entrance.

432.speaker: Sal Ignacius
432.text: "I hope that man is duly punished for his actions. We wouldn't want others following his example."

433.speaker: Sal Ignacius
433.text: "Apart from the Golcondists, we have seen a rising Dastnurist minority due to the growing numbers of migrants from Wehlen and Rumburg."

449.speaker: Player_Romus
449.text: "Fascinating. I'd love to hear more about them."

450.speaker: Player_Romus
450.text: "No time to bother with corpses. We've got a ceremony to perform."

452.speaker: Sal Ignacius
452.text: "We shouldn't delay the ceremony much longer."

453.speaker: Sal Ignacius
453.text: "But very well. Who would you like to know about?"

475.speaker: Narrator
475.text: In an adjacent room, there were several tombs, each adorned with intricate decorations.

476.speaker: Sal Ignacius
476.text: "Here lies Bredus Azaro, the first Duke of Montaklar. All members of the Royal House of Azaro are descended from him."

477.speaker: Sal Ignacius
477.text: "The damage to his tomb was another casualty of the Golcondist pilgrims when a piece of the above ceiling came crashing down."

481.speaker: Sal Ignacius
481.text: "Thanks to the funds that will now be put toward repairs, poor Bredus can finally be re-laid to rest."

483.speaker: Sal Ignacius
483.text: "That would be the tomb of Talerius Azaro. Not only was he the Earl of Havas, he was the most revered general during the War of Rizian Succession."

484.speaker: Sal Ignacius
484.text: "Even though House Azaro ultimately lost the war, the general never lost a single battle."

485.speaker: Sal Ignacius
485.text: "After the war, he established Camp Domus -- Rizia's largest military base to this day."

489.speaker: Narrator
489.text: His mentioning of Camp Domus flooded my mind with fond memories of my time there as a young recruit.

490.speaker: Player_Romus
490.text: "Yes, I'm quite familiar with his reputation."

491.speaker: Player_Romus
491.text: "Even though he fought against House Toras, I still hold him in the highest respect."

492.speaker: Player_Romus
492.text: "He may be revered by some, but I never much cared for him."

493.speaker: Sal Ignacius
493.text: "That would be Aurelia Itxaro. If you remember your history, he was the famed industrialist of the 19th Century whose revolutionary mining equipment led to the Second Rizian Gold Rush."

494.speaker: Sal Ignacius
494.text: "While he isn't of royal lineage, his legacy earned him a place amongst them."

495.speaker: Sal Ignacius
495.text: "He single-handedly brought incomprehensible wealth to this kingdom overnight, granting us enduring power and influence."

497.speaker: Narrator
497.text: He paused with his hand on the door.

502.speaker: Narrator
502.text: Partway up the stairs, I heard Titus and his men apprehending the assailant. Sal hobbled up behind me, panting.

503.speaker: Player_Romus
503.text: "Is that where you keep the torch-er chamber?"

507.speaker: Narrator
507.text: Given his ambivalence towards me, his reply should have come as no surprise.

508.speaker: Narrator
508.text: Though I wished he'd given more insight on what to expect, I respected Father's vow of secrecy and didn't press the issue further.

511.speaker: Narrator
511.text: Eager to follow along, they got louder the higher my hand raised, and quieter when I brought it down low.

512.speaker: Narrator
512.text: The onlookers' enthusiasm diminished as I dismissively made my way past. They clearly had expected a show.

514.speaker: Narrator
514.text: The shouts of admiration resonated even louder from my subjects.

516.speaker: Narrator
516.text: The old Wruhecist proverb translated to "Let joy fill the hearts of those who seek the Lord."

517.speaker: Narrator
517.text: In unison, the crowd shouted, "Lusel Dominatun Deunon; senkusant pactum denborarik!"

523.speaker: Narrator
523.text: Titus quickly exited the vehicle and opened my side door.

524.speaker: Titus Gordion
524.text: "These people look like they could give you trouble. Shall I have them removed?"

526.speaker: Player_Romus
526.text: "You really had to ask? Get those traitors the hell out of my sight."

527.speaker: Player_Romus
527.text: "No, they have the right to protest, even if I disagree with their cause."

528.speaker: Player_Romus
528.text: "Let them protest, Captain, seeing as how this issue holds significant importance to them."

534.speaker: Narrator
534.text: I turned back toward the crowd. They were still applauding me.

537.speaker: Narrator
537.text: He cast an intimidating glare at the protesters as we passed them.

538.speaker: Narrator
538.text: He cast an intimidating glare at the protesters as we passed them.

539.speaker: Narrator
539.text: Captain Gordion quietly spoke to several nearby guards who began herding the protesters away.

540.speaker: Narrator
540.text: The captain barked at several nearby guards to remove the protesters, and they began clearing them out.

543.speaker: Player_Romus
543.text: "I'm tempted to knock to see if anyone's home."

545.speaker: Narrator
545.text: Despite my apprehension, I took his hands.

546.speaker: Player_Romus
546.text: "Fine. The sooner we get this over with the better."

548.speaker: Player_Romus
548.text: "Then I sincerely hope you can find it in your heart to forgive me."

549.speaker: Player_Romus
549.text: "Then I'll be sure to keep that in mind if ever you should come groveling on your knees asking for *my* consent."

550.speaker: Narrator
550.text: The wiscerer went silent. Though he outwardly remained calm, the sliver of vexation in his eyes was undeniable.

551.speaker: Sal Ignacius
551.text: "It's not forgiveness from you that you should be seeking, but forgiveness from God."

552.speaker: Sal Ignacius
552.text: "I must stay here until the visions run their course. Please find your own way out."

553.speaker: Narrator
553.text: He closed his eyes and began trembling. I ignored him, put on my clothes, and made my way back through the catacombs until I'd reach the surface.

556.speaker: Sal Ignacius
556.text: "You only just inherited the throne -- an appointment that comes with the greatest of responsibilities -- so allow me to offer you some advice..."

559.speaker: Player_Romus
559.text: "*Unsolicited* advice. But do go on. I want to hear what you have to say."

560.speaker: Player_Romus
560.text: "Request denied. Good day, Grand Wiseman. I'll see myself out."

562.speaker: Sal Ignacius
562.text: "What I wanted to say was... burn too many bridges -- especially this early into your reign -- and you may find yourself marooned on a deserted shore."

563.speaker: Narrator
563.text: Wary as I was, I relented and did as he requested.

564.speaker: Narrator
564.text: I put on my clothes, and made my way back through the catacombs until I'd reached the surface -- the events of today, forever burned in my memory.

570.speaker: Player_Romus
570.text: "No, I haven't changed my mind about that. However... perhaps we can overlook my abstention?"
570.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_PlavoSanctuaryRestoration_Project"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_SallabesSanctuaryExpansion_Project"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_SallabesSanctuaryExpansion_Project"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Policy_Welfare_PlavoSanctuaryRestoration_Project"] == true) == false)

571.speaker: Sal Ignacius
571.text: "That's asking a lot. The importance of the ceremony cannot be overstated."

572.speaker: Player_Romus
572.text: "What if I made it worth your while?"

573.speaker: Player_Romus
573.text: "What if I told you there would be consequences for defying the king's wishes?"

574.speaker: Sal Ignacius
574.text: "Then I would tell you that repercussions are of no concern to me. I stand on the side of God. Can you say the same?"

575.speaker: Player_Romus
575.text: "Well, Your Holiness, it seems we've reached an impasse. I'll see myself out."

576.speaker: Player_Romus
576.text: "A man with convictions... It's a rarity these days. I respect that. Until next time."

577.speaker: Player_Romus
577.text: "Well then... now that we better understand each other, perhaps we can one day channel that newfound knowledge toward seeing eye to eye."

584.speaker: Player_Romus
584.text: "You're right. Forget what I said. 'Til next time."

586.speaker: Sal Ignacius
586.text: "Make no mistake... In matters of upholding principles, my steadfastness knows no bounds."

587.speaker: Sal Ignacius
587.text: "While I have my reservations about what you're suggesting... My curiosity far outweighs my skepticism."

590.speaker: Player_Romus
590.text: "I look forward to future discussions. Maybe then I can nurture your curiosity even further."

591.speaker: Player_Romus
591.text: "Then I look forward to speaking to you about future... arrangements."

594.speaker: Sal Ignacius
594.text: "That I may be old, but I know which way to move when the wind blows."

595.speaker: Sal Ignacius
595.text: "I look forward to speaking more about this with you at a later date."

596.speaker: Narrator
596.text: The tense interaction with the grand wiseman and the friction that came with it wasn't beneficial for anyone.

597.speaker: Narrator
597.text: As my motorcade journeyed down the highway and the Archsacturary of Plavo gradually disappeared from sight, I reflected on all I had achieved today.

598.speaker: Player_Romus
598.text: "Good to hear. I underestimated you, Your Holiness."

599.speaker: Player_Romus
599.text: "I don't want to be around someone who is so easily swayed. Forget it."

600.speaker: Player_Romus
600.text: "Very good. I look forward to future *arrangements* between us."

603.speaker: Player_Romus
603.text: "As long as the wind continues to blow in the right direction."

604.speaker: Sal Ignacius
604.text: "Yes, of course. Though predicting the weather can be a tricky thing."

606.speaker: Narrator
606.text: I wished Sal goodbye and left the premises. Captain Gordion and his men followed behind.

607.speaker: Sal Ignacius
607.text: "Well, I'm sorry to hear that. However, in the future, I suggest not being so quick to slam the door shut when opportunities present themselves."

609.speaker: Player_Romus
609.text: "As in, any *kindness* bestowed upon me will be reciprocated."

610.speaker: Player_Romus
610.text: "Meaning, I won't feel the need to seek *alternatives* to convince you to be more compliable."

611.speaker: Player_Romus
611.text: "As in, you keep your position as Grand Wiseman and aren't replaced by someone more... agreeable."

612.speaker: Player_Romus
612.text: "That if you do me this one small favor, another small favor will be returned to you should the time come."

614.speaker: Sal Ignacius
614.text: "Do what you must. But I stand on the side of riotousness."

615.speaker: Sal Ignacius
615.text: "Now, now... let's not be hasty. You wouldn't want to do anything that might disrupt the balance between us."

616.speaker: Sal Ignacius
616.text: "If you insist. However, if you get a knock back, I'd suggest we vacate this place as soon as humanly possible."

619.speaker: Sal Ignacius
619.text: "Our departed friends won't be coming back to life anytime soon, in case you were worried."

623.speaker: Sal Ignacius
623.text: "Most amusing. If it's torture you want, the soprano section of the Wruhecist Tabernacle Choir will do the trick."

625.speaker: Player_Romus
625.text: "I'm going to catch the plague, I know it."

627.speaker: Sal Ignacius
627.text: "The path ahead leads us to one of the holiest sites in Wruhecism. Believe me, it has undergone thorough purification."

629.speaker: Sal Ignacius
629.text: "Believe me, this is only the beginning."

635.speaker: Player_Romus
635.text: "I'll look into funding these projects as soon as the Treasury allows it."

636.speaker: Narrator
636.text: The Grand Wiseman clasped his hands together.

638.speaker: Narrator
638.text: We eventually reached an imposing iron door. Behind it was a descending spiral staircase illuminated by torches mounted on the walls.

644.speaker: Narrator
644.text: Decorated in gold, I would have considered it the most splendid of all if not for the hole in the lid, through which I could catch a glimpse of the skeletal remains within.

645.speaker: Player_Romus

(Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn01_Briefing_Religion_Body01"] == true  and

647.speaker: Player_Romus
647.text: "What would a Derdian Golcondist be doing here?"

648.speaker: Narrator
648.text: Dastnurity was the other main branch of the Nurist religion, observed in most countries to our north. Its followers relied on the writings of St. Dast as the only pure scripture.

649.speaker: Sal Ignacius
649.text: "Come. It is time you saw what they did to this very building. "

650.speaker: Player_Romus
650.text: "I have my own ways of honoring God, and this is not one of them."

651.speaker: Player_Romus
651.text: "Well, there's a first time for everything."

652.speaker: Narrator
652.text: But whether or not our little row could be rectified, I would prepare for any eventuality.

657.speaker: Narrator
657.text: Sal closed his eyes and tilted his head up slightly, awaiting my next words.

658.speaker: Narrator
658.text: One was waving a sign that read, "Golcondism Is Not Blasphemy."

662.speaker: Player_Romus
662.text: "Demanding entrance to our sacred Wruhecist space... I hope he gets what's coming to him."

663.speaker: Player_Romus
663.text: "I didn't know Derdia's fundamentalism had gotten this out of control."

664.speaker: Player_Romus
664.text: "I'm not surprised at his actions. When you deprive a man of religious freedom, this is the consequence."

665.speaker: Sal Ignacius
665.text: "It is not 'freedom' that motivates these men, but blood lust."

666.speaker: Sal Ignacius
666.text: "Alas, our Derdian brothers have strayed far from God's path."

667.speaker: Sal Ignacius
667.text: "Do not be too harsh towards our Derdian brothers. They know not what they do."

668.speaker: Sal Ignacius
668.text: "But the more Derdians came to Rizia, the more they overwhelmed the sacred sanctuaries of Plavo, Benievon, and Jales with their blasphemous version of worship."

669.speaker: Sal Ignacius
669.text: "They aim to trace the footsteps of Wruhec's disciples through what is now Merkopa. Which necessitates visiting their final resting places."

670.speaker: Sal Ignacius
670.text: "I did so with a heavy heart. But our sanctuaries are a place of peace. They are not for those who exalt violence."

671.speaker: Sal Ignacius
671.text: "The Golcondists have a martial culture, Your Majesty. They seek purification through violence."

673.speaker: Sal Ignacius
673.text: "But our sanctuaries are places of peace. They are not for those who exalt violence."

677.speaker: Narrator
677.text: I tried to remember Vina taking her first steps, but could not. I must have been absent at the time.

681.speaker: Narrator
681.text: Sal gestured over our heads to the second-floor gallery overlooking the hall. Part of it had collapsed, and the rest had been roped off.

682.speaker: Player_Romus
682.text: "I have to say, the disheveled look gives the place character."

683.speaker: Player_Romus
683.text: "It looks to have seen better days."

684.speaker: Player_Romus
684.text: "It's a shame what happened to such a magnificent building."

690.speaker: Narrator
690.text: Sal began to pace around the altar.

691.speaker: Sal Ignacius
691.text: "Rizia's religious climate is at a crossroads, Your Majesty."

692.speaker: Sal Ignacius
692.text: "From aiding the impoverished to expanding educational opportunities, our faith-based institutions are a cornerstone of everyday life, strengthening the bonds that hold our society together."

693.speaker: Sal Ignacius
693.text: "All under the umbrella of our state religion, Wruhecism."

694.speaker: Player_Romus
694.text: “As it should be. I know I’d be lost without Wruhecism to show me the way.”

696.speaker: Player_Romus
696.text: "Should religion really be playing such a large role in modern society?"

698.speaker: Player_Romus
698.text: "You could have fooled me. I look around and I see heretics and blasphemers everywhere."

703.speaker: Player_Romus
703.text: "You are forgetting religion's most important role of all. That of pacifying the populace."

704.speaker: Sal Ignacius
704.text: "Our modern world is fractured, Your Majesty. Morality is faltering. We need God more than ever."

706.speaker: Sal Ignacius
706.text: "Indeed, our religious unity has begun to splinter in recent years."

707.speaker: Sal Ignacius
707.text: "But our religious unity has begun to splinter in recent years."

708.speaker: Sal Ignacius
708.text: "Surely you have noticed our religious unity beginning to splinter."

709.speaker: Sal Ignacius
709.text: "It is true that sharing a single belief system fosters unity among our people."

710.speaker: Sal Ignacius
710.text: "But sadly, that unity has begun to splinter in recent years."

711.speaker: Narrator
711.text: Lena had been a follower, but converted to Wruhecism on joining the Rizian royal family.

715.speaker: Narrator
715.text: A sacrifice, but one she gladly made in order to be with me.

716.speaker: Narrator
716.text: Her resentment over the sacrifice was palpable throughout our marriage.

717.speaker: Sal Ignacius
717.text: "I would never counsel this country to turn away people in need, Your Majesty. But I do worry that our Wruhecist values are in danger of becoming diluted."

722.speaker: Player_Romus
722.text: "I'll be honest with you. I don't particularly care."

723.speaker: Sal Ignacius
723.text: "Many in this country do, Your Majesty. Ask your uncle."

724.speaker: Narrator
724.text: He stopped pacing and looked around the hall.

725.speaker: Narrator
725.text: He pointed once more to the balcony.

726.speaker: Sal Ignacius
726.text: "The Crown has funded and nurtured religious institutions since our kingdom's very founding. And for good reason."

727.speaker: Sal Ignacius
727.text: "No Rizian king or queen has ever rejected the holy consecration."

735.speaker: Narrator
735.text: Having memorized them years ago, I recited them in unison.

736.speaker: Narrator
736.text: He slowly fed the words to me, and I repeated them back.

738.speaker: Sal Ignacius
738.text: "Only the most pious and reverent of men may drink from the sacred chalice, Your Majesty."

743.speaker: Narrator
743.text: We continued towards the archsanctuary's entrance.

744.speaker: Sal Ignacius
744.text: "You made the right decision in removing the protesters, Your Majesty. We would not have wanted them disrupting our ceremony."

745.speaker: Player_Romus
745.text: "'Golcondism Is Not Blasphemy?' How dare they challenge our religious laws?'"

747.speaker: Sal Ignacius
747.text: "Definitely Golcondists. Derdian ones, judging by their garb."

748.speaker: Player_Romus
748.text: "The guards went too easy on them. They should have locked up the whole lot."

750.speaker: Player_Romus
750.text: "Those poor lost souls. Is there any hope for them?"

751.speaker: Sal Ignacius
751.text: "The Golcondists have been irate ever since we began denying them entrance to 'their' holy sites."

752.speaker: Sal Ignacius
752.text: "Be not too harsh on our Derdian Golcondist brethren. They may yet find their way back to the path of righteousness."

756.speaker: Sal Ignacius
756.text: "Only if they give up their twisted form of Wruhecism and return to the correct path."

757.speaker: Sal Ignacius
757.text: "A large group of Golcondists came here on one of their holy pilgrimages from Derdia several years ago. An argument with the local Wruhecist worshippers led to an... altercation."

758.speaker: Player_Romus
758.text: "Those beasts. Praise the Lord it won't happen again."

759.speaker: Player_Romus
759.text: "Are you sure the locals didn't start it? The inhabitants of Cardesse-Montaklar are not exactly conflict-averse."

760.speaker: Player_Romus
760.text: "That's the only reason for our blasphemy law?"

761.speaker: Player_Romus
761.text: "And why has it not been fixed since then?"

762.speaker: Sal Ignacius
762.text: "It was the feather that tipped the scale, so to speak."

764.speaker: Sal Ignacius
764.text: "I assure you, the warrior culture of the Derdians makes the Azaros look meek."

765.speaker: Sal Ignacius
765.text: "Halaita. If it is said, so it is, so it will be."

770.speaker: Sal Ignacius
770.text: "That will not be you. At least not today."

771.speaker: Sal Ignacius
771.text: "That will not be you. Not today, and possibly not ever."

772.speaker: Player_Romus
772.text: "This ceremony has exceeded the limits of reason. I cannot participate in good conscience."

773.speaker: Sal Ignacius
773.text: "This not a promising start to your reign."

777.speaker: Sal Ignacius
777.text: "I sense skepticism in you, Your Majesty. But please know that as the King of Rizia, the will of the Divine now courses through your veins."

778.speaker: Sal Ignacius
778.text: "It is your responsibility to carry out what He has ordained. And it is mine to aid you in your holy duty."

779.speaker: Sal Ignacius
779.text: "Surely you now feel it, Your Majesty. The will of the Divine coursing through your veins."

780.speaker: Player_Romus
780.text: "It is a heavy burden, Grand Wiseman. But I accept it."

781.speaker: Player_Romus
781.text: "I am an instrument of nobody. Not God, and definitely not you."

782.speaker: Player_Romus
782.text: "I pray that He and you will guide me to do what is best for our country."

783.speaker: Player_Romus
783.text: "I must confess that I'm not entirely convinced about what transpired here today. But if it helps appease the masses, count me in."

787.speaker: Sal Ignacius
787.text: "You will see the light one day. I am confident of it."

789.speaker: Narrator
789.text: I nodded in agreement at the ancient Wruhecist term. It was short for "Decensi halaita veretan": "If it is said, so it is, so it will be."

796.speaker: Narrator
796.text: Only a select few, such as Grand Wiseman and religious councilor Sal Ignacius, were privy to what the ceremony entailed.

797.speaker: Narrator
797.text: As I stepped out and onto the pavement, I was immediately greeted by the roar of a crowd that had come to witness my arrival.

798.speaker: Narrator
798.text: I performed variations of this toward different sections of the crowd, much to their amusement.

799.speaker: Narrator
799.text: It was the traditional reply meaning, "He is the Lord our God; his covenant is everlasting."

800.speaker: Sal Ignacius
800.text: "I know he wished to return this sacred Wruhecist site to its former grandeur. He agreed with me that state funds should be allocated for the project."

801.speaker: Narrator
801.text: Amidst the commotion, one managed to slip from their grasp and dashed towards me with frightening speed.

802.speaker: Narrator
802.text: After my flesh was fully coated, he set aside the jug and sponge, reaching for the chalice and bottle of wine.

803.speaker: Narrator
803.text: If it was, did I accept the responsibility that came with my consecration?

804.speaker: Sal Ignacius
804.text: "That's the gift and the curse that comes with the divine right of the king."

805.speaker: Narrator
805.text: Did I really speak for the Divine?

806.speaker: Sal Ignacius
806.text: "A lamb... I see a charming little lamb..."

811.speaker: Narrator
811.text: He paused, deep in thought, then let out a small laugh, smiling to himself.

812.speaker: Narrator
812.text: He paused, deep in thought, then let out a small laugh.

813.speaker: Sal Ignacius
813.text: "Once separated from its flock by a great wolf, it now reunites with them."

815.speaker: Player_Romus
815.text: "Bringing the faithful back into the fold, perhaps?"

818.speaker: Sal Ignacius
818.text: "Interrupting the ritual will have long-lasting consequences."

819.speaker: Narrator
819.text: There was a flash of irritation in his eyes.

820.speaker: Sal Ignacius
820.text: "More often than not, friends and foes are indistinguishable from one another."

821.speaker: Player_Romus
821.text: "Unless you're aiming for a medieval revival of the Dark Ages..."

823.speaker: Player_Romus
823.text: "Now if you'll excuse me, I'll see myself out."

825.speaker: Sal Ignacius
825.text: "But in light of your generous support, I see no reason why the public has to no any differently."

826.speaker: Sal Ignacius
826.text: "However, keeping an open mind through curiosity and skepticism lies at the heart of Wruhecism."

827.speaker: Sal Ignacius
827.text: "That would be much appreciated, Your Majesty."

828.speaker: Sal Ignacius
828.text: "The only convincing you need isn't from me but from God. And He isn't so easily swayed."

833.speaker: Narrator
833.text: I nodded in agreement at the ancient Wruhecist term.

839.speaker: Sal Ignacius
839.text: "Rightly so. Nobody should attack the King of Rizia, especially not for upholding our religious laws."

841.speaker: Player_Romus
841.text: “He got all this just for *teaching*? My own final resting place had better be even grander."

842.speaker: Sal Ignacius
842.text: "To use one's wisdom to enlighten others is to do the Lord's work."

844.speaker: Sal Ignacius
844.text: "I would like to think I am honoring Caelus the Devout's legacy by passing my own limited knowledge to you."

850.speaker: Player_Romus
850.text: “The holy books do tell of mystical events occurring on this site, but they are unclear as to their nature."

851.speaker: Sal Ignacius
851.text: “I shall enlighten you. This is where Caelus received the gift of foresight."

852.speaker: Sal Ignacius
852.text: “I refer to the miracle of foresight."

853.speaker: Sal Ignacius
853.text: "I have spent the past weeks cloistered here, fasting and praying, in order to transform myself into a vessel for the visions."

854.speaker: Player_Romus
854.text: "Having said that... can't you overlook my abstention? I don't want news getting out that I refused this rite."

855.speaker: Sal Ignacius
855.text: "Are you asking a holy man to lie, Your Majesty?"

856.speaker: Sal Ignacius
856.text: "You prioritized it over Plavo's restoration, despite my advice. And you wish to be rewarded for it?"

866.speaker: Narrator
866.text: One of the Grand Wiseman priests handed him a wooden case.

867.speaker: Sal Ignacius
867.text: "In honor of this momentous day, I would like to bestow upon you one of the most sacred Nurist relics in Rizia."

868.speaker: Narrator
868.text: He opened the case to reveal an intricately decorated scepter.

870.speaker: Sal Ignacius
870.text: "It was said that before the time of St. Wruhec, master artisan Dorian Etxeberria had a vivid dream in which St. Dast appeared, urging him to create the scepter to encapsulate the Pillars of Nurity."

871.speaker: Sal Ignacius
871.text: "Driven by this divine vision, Dorian meticulously designed and forged the scepter, believing it to be his sacred duty to honor the saint's legacy."

872.speaker: Sal Ignacius
872.text: "And now, I give it to you."

873.speaker: Player_Romus
873.text: "I shall wield this with pride, so all who see me will be reminded that I walk in Nur's holy light."

874.speaker: Player_Romus
874.text: "A reminder that while we espouse the six tenets of Wruhecism now, it was St. Dast who created the original foundations of our faith."

875.speaker: Player_Romus
875.text: "I am deeply humbled and profoundly grateful for this extraordinary honor."

878.speaker: Player_Romus
878.text: "I'm honored, but I believe it would be better suited under your esteemed care and guardianship."

879.speaker: Player_Romus
879.text: "Thanks, but I have enough scepters. You keep it."

880.speaker: Player_Romus
880.text: "I appreciate the gesture, but I'm not worthy of such a gift."

884.speaker: Sal Ignacius
884.text: "Sanctuaries such as this one are at the core of our religious communities. Without a place to congregate, the faithful are left wandering without guidance."

885.speaker: Sal Ignacius
885.text: "And I am sorry to say your father -- Nur bless his soul -- left us with quite a bit of work to do with regard to their upkeep."

886.speaker: Sal Ignacius
886.text: "Afraid of angering one religious group by prioritizing the needs of the other, he funded neither."

887.speaker: Sal Ignacius
887.text: "This may be true, but Wehlen and Rumburg are both watching our treatment of Dastnurists closely."

888.speaker: Sal Ignacius
888.text: "Focusing on the restoration of Plavo will strengthen our domestic Wruhecist community, but ignoring the plight of Dastnurists may damage our international standing."

892.speaker: Player_Romus
892.text: "You brought me here to make a funding decision, under the guise of a ritual? The greed of the Sanctuary truly knows no bounds."

893.speaker: Narrator
893.text: The holy man withdrew, looking hurt.

894.speaker: Sal Ignacius
894.text: "My intention was not to pressure you, only to inform you of the situation."

895.speaker: Sal Ignacius
895.text: "But now that you have seen the state Plavo is in, I am sure you understand how urgently it must be restored."

896.speaker: Player_Romus
896.text: "We are in a holy place, Grand Wiseman. I refuse to sully it with deliberations over finances."

897.speaker: Narrator
897.text: The holy man drew in his breath.

898.speaker: Sal Ignacius
898.text: "You are absolutely right, Your Majesty. Now is not the time to speak of such vulgar things as money."

900.speaker: Player_Romus
900.text: "Don't worry, Plavo will get its funding. But next time, come straight out and ask me." [-2 Budget]

906.speaker: Player_Romus
906.text: "Quite the contrary. Plavo can wait. I'll allocate funds for that Dastnurist Grandsanctuary you mentioned." [-2 Budget]

908.speaker: Player_Romus
908.text: "I understand when I'm being manipulated. Don't bother me with these requests again."

910.speaker: Sal Ignacius
910.text: "I won't, Your Majesty. I am sorry."

911.speaker: Player_Romus
911.text: "I prefer it this way. It reminds one that God is as capable of destruction as He is of creation."

912.speaker: Sal Ignacius
912.text: "Y-yes, it is beautiful in its own way..."

913.speaker: Sal Ignacius
913.text: "At any rate, I will trouble you with this no further. It is almost time for the ceremony."

914.speaker: Sal Ignacius
914.text: “If you'll allow me, we shall proceed with the Consecration of the King ceremony."

915.speaker: Sal Ignacius
915.text: "This is a most auspicious start to today's ceremony. And God willing, it is only the beginning of Rizia's religious renaissance."

916.speaker: Sal Ignacius
916.text: "Let us proceed with your consecration at once."

917.speaker: Sal Ignacius
917.text: "For now, let us proceed with your consecration."

918.speaker: Player_Romus
918.text: "Luckily for you, the well-being of Rizia's religious communities is important to me. I will consider your requests."

920.speaker: Sal Ignacius
920.text: "Most kind of you, Your Majesty. Thank you."

921.speaker: Player_Romus
921.text: "A commoner, buried among the Montaklar nobility? What an insult."

922.speaker: Player_Romus
922.text: "A pioneer to whom we all owe a debt of gratitude. Rizia could use more innovators like him."

923.speaker: Player_Romus
923.text: "It's his fault Rizia became so reliant on resources. Perhaps we would have been better off leaving that gold in the ground."

924.speaker: Sal Ignacius
924.text: "As long as they remember that it is by the Lord's grace, not man's, that Rizia is blessed with such abundant resources."

925.speaker: Sal Ignacius
925.text: "The Lord put that gold in the ground to enrich our nation, Your Majesty. So that we may better exalt His good name."

926.speaker: Sal Ignacius
926.text: "With the love of God in his heart, any man can achieve greatness. No matter how lowborn."

931.speaker: Player_Romus
931.text: "This represents Dast's eleven pillars, not Wruhec's six core tenets. Dastnurists will see it as an endorsement of their faith."

933.speaker: Sal Ignacius
933.text: "I see the scepter as a reminder of our shared Nurist origins. Our Wruhec refined the teachings of St. Dast. He did not contradict them."

937.speaker: Sal Ignacius
937.text: "The more robust our many religious communities are, the greater the tithings we can collect for the monarchy."

938.speaker: Sal Ignacius
938.text: "To put it in earthly terms... keep Rizia's faithful happy, and new sanctuaries will pay for themselves."

939.speaker: Player_Romus
939.text: “Why was he so afraid of angering Dastnurists? They make up only a small part of the population, after all."

943.speaker: Sal Ignacius
943.text: "Rightfully so, considering the state of our treasury."

944.speaker: Sal Ignacius
944.text: "Considering the state of our treasury, I don't know what he was worried about."

953.speaker: Sal Ignacius
953.text: "With the entire religious community's attention on today's ceremony, there will never be a more opportune time to sign the order. And from there, we can construct new sanctuaries all over the land..."

954.speaker: Player_Romus
954.text: "So that more people may bask in God's glory."

955.speaker: Player_Romus
955.text: "I get what you're saying. If we keep our people busy with religion, we won't have to worry about them turning against us."

956.speaker: Player_Romus
956.text: "The Crown's money should be spent on improving our citizens' welfare, regardless of their religion."

959.speaker: Sal Ignacius
959.text: "Spreading the great word of Nur is my goal, Your Majesty. Not pacification."

960.speaker: Sal Ignacius
960.text: "But you are right that our citizens are less likely to stir up turmoil when their spiritual needs are met."

961.speaker: Sal Ignacius
961.text: "Do not neglect the importance of spiritual welfare, Your Majesty."

962.speaker: Sal Ignacius
962.text: "A pity. With enough funds, you and I could build new sanctuaries all across the land..."

963.speaker: Player_Romus
963.text: "I aim to transform Rizia into a strong, modern nation. I'm not going to waste time catering to the whims of its fanatics."

964.speaker: Sal Ignacius
964.text: "The majority of our citizens hold Nurist beliefs, Your Majesty. You won't get far by calling them 'fanatics'."

972.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
972.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.SanctuaryQHub_Dastnurists"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.SanctuaryQHub_Budget"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.SanctuaryQHub_ReligiousRevenues"] == true) == false

988.speaker: Player_Romus
988.text: "Such a grand expenditure would certainly drain the Crown of its resources."

990.speaker: Sal Ignacius
990.text: "Indeed... I am afraid both of these projects will be quite costly endeavors."

994.speaker: Sal Ignacius
994.text: "But we have enough funds to get started on the Plavo restoration already. And with the entire religious community's attention on today's ceremony, there will never be a more opportune time to sign the order."

995.speaker: Sal Ignacius
995.text: "But we do have the funds in place, Your Majesty. And with the entire religious community's attention on today's ceremony, there will never be a more opportune time to sign the order."

999.speaker: Sal Ignacius
999.text: "From there, you and I can build new sanctuaries all across the land..."

1000.speaker: Sal Ignacius
1000.text: "But I urge you not to neglect either of them. Even if they cannot be funded right away."

1002.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
1002.text: Gesture for him to keep going.

1004.speaker: Sal Ignacius
1004.text: "But neglect them, and unrest could follow. Four decades ago, reforms stirred discontent that began in sanctuaries and spilled into the streets."

1005.speaker: Sal Ignacius
1005.text: "When the faithful grow uneasy, their tithes shrink, leaving the Crown to fill the gap."
